extracted.intended_audience: deans, chairpersons, and faculty members in vocational and technical education programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for developing, writing, and submitting grant proposals to obtain funds or donated equipment for vocational/technical and other educational programs, including needs assessment, funder selection, proposal content, budgets, timelines, and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess program needs / needs-assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Before starting to search for potential funding sources, a full assessment of program equipment needs should be prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine and describe program objectives in terms of student learning outcomes and contributions to the community; explain concrete additional program gains if equipment needs are fulfilled; show how equipment will provide state-of-the-art training; develop a summary model showing where funding will be used; identify current funding and insufficiencies; list needs as one-time vs continuous; develop rationale based on enrollment projections, technological update requirements, and special learning goals; compile data to support requests; document past use of funds to show effective stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select funding sources / fit with funder priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Select funding sources that are most likely to award grants based on the program needs and the funder's purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use directories and funder materials to learn purpose, structure, funding priorities, proposal requirements, schedule, award sizes and deadlines; determine applicant eligibility; ask whether preliminary concept papers are preferred; clarify total funding available, typical award size, number of awards, partial awards policy, and cyclical deadlines; explore special strengthening features (matching funds, private sector support); contact past applicants and other institutions for insights; request grant application packages and read them carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funder format and application instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the format requested by the funding agency or copy the format used in previous successful proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all required pieces, use the provided forms, and avoid extraneous or expensive-looking brochures or enclosures which may send the wrong message about cost concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write clear, concise, and non‑technical prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid obscure language and convoluted writing so narrative is understandable to laypersons as well as experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the key concept in one sentence; keep key ideas concise; avoid overly complex or many alternative approaches (may appear unfocused); present confident language—avoid 'ifs', 'buts', and 'maybes'; make the main idea clearly and logically presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define measurable program objectives and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Write program objectives in terms of measurable results that reflect important outcomes for students, faculty, the institution, and/or the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think of program results that would make good newspaper stories; show how requested funds will enable meeting objectives; include quantifiable targets, timetables, and evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate need with reliable data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use data, especially numbers and graphs, to support needs, timetables, specific evaluation plans, and budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data should come from reliable sources; show cost per student over time to highlight return on investment; compile enrollment, job-placement records, and other supporting statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a convincing budget and cost justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a clear budget showing how funds will be used and assurances that funds will be spent wisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify each cost item and include indirect costs; indicate in-kind or matching resources; include budget categories (salaries, benefits, consultants, travel, equipment, supplies, subcontracting, indirect costs, total direct/total costs); ensure budget reflects project scope; prepare budget worksheet and business-office review; avoid requesting unrealistic amounts relative to proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show organizational capacity and track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the applicant organization's resources, past experience, and ability to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a capacity statement and management/monitoring systems; document prior effective use of funds; include resumes of key personnel and evidence of institutional support and administrative approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff qualifications and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe who will staff the project, their experience, credentials, amount of effort and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include personnel utilization matrix or person-months table; show how staff roles align with tasks and phases; attach clear, readable resumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan of action / implementation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain what will be done, the order of events, techniques and processes to be used, relationship and outcome of each element, timeline and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include activity-task planning schedule, project timeline with milestones and deliverables, and indicate phasing; make plan logically sequenced and feasible within the funding period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a project timeline showing phases, milestones, interfaces, and deliverables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use graphical timelines or Gantt-like charts; align personnel utilization and budget to timeline; indicate key dates and expected completion points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and monitoring plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the project will be monitored, measured, and evaluated; what data will be collected and how it will be analyzed and interpreted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify evaluation methods, performance indicators, frequency of measurement, responsible parties, and how evaluation results will inform project adjustments and report to funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and equipment description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the facilities and equipment needed and available, equipment to be purchased, its use, benefit and expected life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how new equipment integrates with existing facilities; justify equipment choices and expected useful life; discuss maintenance and replacement plans if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate external support and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Show evidence of support from outside volunteers, advisory panels, businesses, civic organizations, and other stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include letters of support, advisory committee endorsements, evidence of in-kind contributions, vendor/manufacturer involvement, and plans for private-sector partnerships to strengthen the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching funds and in‑kind contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: List matching funds and explain how they will be combined with requested support to maximize impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State amounts/types of match, source (institutional, private-sector, foundations), percent match requirements (e.g., SME required 50%-50% for capital equipment), and how matching increases funder confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and institutional approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether your institution is an eligible applicant and secure necessary administrative approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check funder's eligibility rules; use institutional sign-off schedule (administrative approval to write, budget submission, administrative review and signatures); list proposal manager and reviewers; ensure business office coordination for budgeting and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal completeness and required components
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the proposal includes all required sections (title page, abstract, background, objectives, plan, staff, facilities, evaluation, budget, capacity statement, resumes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided 'Outline of a Typical Proposal' and proposal checklist/evaluation form to self-review completeness; follow pagination/copy instructions (number of copies) and submission formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise abstract and title information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise abstract summarizing the request, significance, objectives, methods, and evaluation plan; include a complete title page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title page should give project title, funding source, initiator, project director, funding period, total funds requested, and date submitted; abstract should clearly and quickly convey the project's essence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity about allowable uses and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and respect funder programmatic restrictions on the use of funds (what is allowable/not allowable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult funder application materials and federal/state program rules (e.g., JTPA or Perkins Act limits) to ensure equipment costs and other line items comply with policies; seek local fund administrator guidance when ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid risky or unfocused proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not propose risky ventures or present too many alternative approaches that may suggest lack of focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate confidence in approach and outcomes; propose feasible, reasonably low-risk activities with clear management and evaluation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and cost-sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a professional proposal without extravagant or costly enclosures that could signal poor cost-sensitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid expensive-looking brochures; be mindful that presentation can influence reviewers' perceptions of fiscal responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and follow-up after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow up your proposal with appropriate communications to the sponsoring organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If questions arise, contact funder representatives; seek corrective feedback if not funded and revise/resubmit; inquire about application status and respond to funder requests promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand grant program types and award sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that grant programs vary by size and type (minigrant vs major grant) and that preparation effort should align with award size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minigrants typically range from several hundred to several thousand dollars; major grants can be thousands to tens of thousands (or larger); match level of proposal detail and institutional commitment to expected award size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research funders and use reference sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use directories and publications (Foundation Directory, Foundation Grants Index, Corporate 500, Annual Guide to Department of Education Programs, Federal Register, Commerce Business Daily) to find and learn about funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain grant application packages, annual reports, and program policies; check local libraries and The Foundation Center; maintain a resource file with contacts, types of funding, and records of outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit help from vendors and manufacturers
rubrics_metrics.description: Involve equipment manufacturers’ representatives early in planning to get technical advice and possible donations or discounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendors can help anticipate future needs and offer in-kind donations or excess inventory; coordinate vendor involvement transparently and document any in-kind support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proposal development and sign-off schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a stepwise development schedule with milestones for drafts, budget preparation, reviews, administrative sign-offs, and final submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document responsibilities (proposal manager/writer/reviewer), dates, reviewer critique and returns, final technical and budget completion, camera-ready copy, duplication and mailing logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide required number of copies and meet deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to funder instructions about number of copies, submission format, and deadline timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some foundations request one copy, others multiple (e.g., eight copies); boards may meet quarterly or monthly—plan submission accordingly; note cyclical deadlines and board meeting schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate broader impact / multi-stakeholder benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that outcomes will be of value to more than one group—students, faculty, institution, and the community/economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight community economic development links, workforce readiness, partnerships with local industry, and scalability/replicability of the program.
